doc.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Driving lesson for Lennie Tristano and his games
summary: Bauer let Tristano drive his car at 3 a.m. and recalls his skill at bar games.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: I think I read something about you giving Lennie Tristano a driving lesson?
Is that one of those — did you really? And there was no accident at the end of it?
No. I think I told Bill Crow, I guess it was Bill Crow—
I says he wasn’t a very good pupil.

Well because Lennie, you know like we were pretty friendly, not in music as much as just two people. And I guess he had, I don’t know maybe it was that way, but he’d talk about average things you know. Like what would we really like to do you know. I mean if you really, what would you — he says, “I’d like to drive the car.” That’s how that come up. Well I felt, well some day, at three o’clock in the morning, I’m alone on the road, I’ll let you drive. And I did. Well like all of those things. But I used to talk to him. We’d have a © Fillius Jazz Archive -21-

thing, he’d shut all the lights out in the room to see if I could compete with him on his deal. And then he’d beat me in these games in the bars, with the little puck, the bowling you know? He bowled a strike, I says, “How’d you do that?” I knew how he did it because he goes down and he measure the length of the board, and the width of it, and you know he feels it, and then he throws it.
